subject: Business Models
title: One-Time Purchase Model
description: A quick, practical guide to One-Time Purchase Model.

hook.text: The simplest revenue model: make something, sell it once, keep the profit. Done.

buildup.text: From lemonade stands to luxury cars, the one-time purchase has dominated commerce for millennia.

discovery.text: The challenge is customer acquisition cost. You must find a new buyer for every single sale.

twist.text: Apple sells you a phone once, then locks you into an ecosystem of recurring app and service revenue.

climax.text: Pure one-time sales are rare now. Most companies layer subscriptions or add-ons on top.

punchline.text: Sell once, earn once. That's why subscriptions took over.

quiz.question: What is the main weakness of a one-time purchase model?
options: Need to acquire new buyers constantly

details.summary: The one-time purchase model charges a single upfront payment for perpetual product ownership. Traditional software licenses, physical goods, and downloadable content all use this approach. Revenue comes entirely from initial sales rather than ongoing subscriptions.
details.whyItMatters: One-time purchases are being replaced by subscriptions across many industries, but they remain dominant for physical goods, games, and customers who resist recurring commitments..
takeaways: Revenue is earned entirely at the point of initial sale
Customers prefer ownership and dislike ongoing payment obligations
Businesses must continuously acquire new customers to maintain revenue

faq.question: Why are companies shifting from one-time purchases to subscriptions?
faq.answer: Subscriptions generate predictable recurring revenue, increase customer lifetime value, enable continuous product updates, and create stronger investor valuations. Adobe's switch from selling Creative Suite for $2,600 to charging $55 monthly increased total revenue dramatically.

faq.question: When should businesses keep the one-time purchase model?
faq.answer: When customers strongly prefer ownership, when the product does not require ongoing service, when the market resists subscriptions, or when the product naturally has a single-use lifecycle. Video games, physical products, and specialized tools often work best as one-time purchases.
